notes: Own implementation (L1-C, committed in ef51676): BLOCK_DEFS covers all 64 BLOCK ids and ITEM_DEFS covers every ITEM id, both keyed exactly to core-types so blockDefs.test.ts / itemDefs.test.ts fail on any missing, duplicate or renamed id. BlockRegistry and ItemRegistry are built from those tables (byId throws RangeError on unknown ids, tryById returns undefined) and expose isSolid / isFullCube / layerOf / lightPropsOf / maxStackOf.

Block entities: chest (27 slots, insert/take/count/drain with stack limits from the item registry), furnace and crafting table payloads, doors (two halves placed and broken together, toggle plus powered state) and beds (foot/head pair, sleep sets the respawn point, respawnPositionFor falls back to a free neighbour when the bed is covered, and mining either half clears the respawn). serializeBlockEntities / deserializeBlockEntities round-trip through index-ascending SerializedBlockEntity records.
BlockDef.itemId === 0 (AIR) is the encoding for 'no item form'; blocks with no item drop nothing. This is asserted in blockDefs.test.ts rather than assuming every block has an item.
support/ provides the BlockEntityWorld abstraction plus createMemoryWorld, the seam that let block entities, redstone and persistence be built in parallel against one interface.

Parallel split: two L2 subagents on their own worktrees and branches, no shared paths. gameplay-b owned src/inventory/** and src/crafting/**; gameplay-c owned src/persistence/** and src/redstone/**. packages/gameplay/src/index.ts was reserved for this branch, so both L2 barrels were wired in here at merge time (dc04d4e and 9df4b62).

Both L2 branches were verified independently before merging rather than trusted from their self-reports: git diff --name-only against ef51676 confirmed NO_OUT_OF_SCOPE for each (only their owned subtrees plus their own report file, no core-types, docs/orchestration, root config, CI or package.json changes), and all four checks were re-run here after each git merge --no-ff.

Naming collisions across the parallel work were avoided by gameplay-b renaming its exports to StackLimitResolver and cloneItemStack so they do not clash with the blockEntities barrel's MaxStackResolver and cloneStack. The full-barrel typecheck at 9df4b62 confirms no duplicate re-exports (TS2308) across all eight modules.

Acceptance coverage at head: 131 gameplay tests in 10 files. Inventory 36 slots (9 hotbar + 27 main) with stack limits, tool durability and survival/creative switching; crafting matchCrafting on both 2x2 and 3x3 with shaped translation invariance and order-independent shapeless matching over 53 recipes; smelting on FURNACE_DEFAULT_COOK_TICKS with fuel consumption, output slot and interrupt/resume that does not corrupt progress; ChunkCodec round trips for palettes 1/2/3/16/17/256/257, all-empty chunks and water-filled chunks with bits in {0,1,2,4,8,16} and no word straddling; WorldStore on IndexedDB plus memory and fs adapters with [worldId, cx, cz] compound keys and 32-chunk / 1500 ms batching; redstone wire decay from 15, levers, buttons, pressure plates, door linkage and pistons converging within REDSTONE.maxUpdatesPerTick with no infinite loops.

fake-indexeddb was already a root devDependency, and the IndexedDB tests pick it up via import 'fake-indexeddb/auto' plus an injectable IDBFactory, so no package.json dependency change was needed and none was made.

All work ran in the gha mcp runner env linux-0jtv23c8; every check result above is an exit code from a job with state=exited and eof=true, not a self-assessment.
